The left panel (A) shows a sample of skin after removal of dermal tissue with a scalpel, and the right panel (B) shows a sample before such treatment. Dashed line indicates the treatment border. Figures A and B show microscopic views of skin from the ankle of a 43-year-old man (WS-2) and the lower leg of a 41-year-old man (WS-7), respectively. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Clinical photographs of elbow ulcers in four Werner syndrome patients (WS1-4); the caption states the skin around the ulcers is sclerotic and atrophic, i.e. a scleroderma-like cutaneous change of WS. Real patient images of a specific WS manifestation. B: Radiographs of the ulcerated elbows in the same four WS patients showing periarticular/subcutaneous soft-tissue calcification, a recognized WS manifestation. C: HE-stained skin from around the elbow ulcers showing strong dermal fibrosis (hyalinized/sclerotic collagen) in all cases, with visible epidermal thinning; characteristic WS histology. D: Higher-magnification HE sections showing calcification within dermal luminal (vascular/lymphatic) structures in WS2-4 together with strong dermal fibrosis; the article title links the calcification to lymphatic-vessel aging.

panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph of a Werner syndrome patient showing the classic progeroid phenotype: bird-like facial gestalt with beak-shaped nose, premature graying and scarcity of hair/eyebrows, thin upper limbs with decreased subcutaneous fat, and truncal obesity. All major visible manifestations map directly to configured Werner syndrome findings; truncal obesity is added as a proposed finding as it is not in the vocabulary.

in_text_mentions: On initial physical examination, he appeared much older than his age with “bird-like” facial appearance, beak-shaped nose, and bilateral cataracts, his voice was high-pitched and his hair and eyebrows were scarce and markedly gray. He had thin upper limbs with decreased subcutaneous fat and truncal obesity (Figure 1). Moreover, we found short stature, hypogenitalism, lower limbs with markedly atrophied skin and subcutaneous fat, abnormal pigmentation of the skin and hyperkeratosis, and flat feet (Figures 2 and 3).
